title: Why Can't You Pat Your Head and Rub Your TUMMY? 🤚
description:
Try it: pat your head with one hand, rub your tummy in circles with the other... now swap. Tangled? Your brain mails every order to BOTH hands: a faint copy of each command meant for one hand leaks to the other (scientists call it neural cross-talk), so your brain has to block that copy, again and again, to let your hands do two different things. That blocking is the strain you feel. Little kids can't block it well yet: when a young child squeezes one hand, the other hand often squeezes too ("mirror movements"), and that fades by about age 10 as the bridge between the two halves of the brain matures. Going faster makes it harder still. Could you swap? Yes or no?
